title: Not All Drift Is a Mechanism: Tracing Prompt Adaptation in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.18412v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Prompt-based adaptation offers several ways to specialize a frozen language model, ranging from natural-language prompt optimization to learned continuous prompts. These methods are usually compared through downstream performance, although similar outputs need not arise from similar internal computations. We study how discrete prompt optimization, prompt tuning, and prefix tuning alter the processing of dense and mixture-of-experts language models. Our analysis shows that the location of the adaptation predicts how task information is carried to the output: optimized text primarily changes response construction, input-level prompts write their influence into content representations, and layer-wise prefixes maintain direct control through attention. translated_title: 并非所有漂移都是机制：追踪大语言模型中的提示词适配
translated_abstract: 基于提示词的适配提供了多种将冻结的语言模型进行专门化的方法，范围涵盖从自然语言提示词优化到学习得到的连续提示词。这些方法通常通过下游性能来进行比较，但相似的输出未必源于相似的内部计算过程。我们研究了离散提示词优化、提示词调优和前缀调优如何改变密集语言模型和混合专家语言模型的内部处理过程。我们的分析表明，适配的位置能够预测任务信息如何被传递到输出：优化后的文本主要改变响应的构建方式，输入层面的提示词将其影响写入内容表示中，而逐层的前缀则通过注意力机制维持对模型的直接控制。在混合专家模型中，这些差异进一步诱导出不同的专家路由模式。与此同时，常见的表示层面度量方法对一般性的上下文变化反应强烈……
tldr: 该论文揭示不同提示词适配方法通过截然不同的内部机制影响大语言模型——适配位置决定了任务信息的传递路径，且在混合专家模型中会引发不同的专家路由模式，表明仅有性能或表示层面的漂移并不足以证明机制相似。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that different prompt adaptation methods affect LLMs through distinct internal mechanisms, where the location of adaptation determines how task information is carried to the output and induces different expert-routing patterns in MoE models, showing that representation-level drift alone does not imply mechanistic similarity.
